answer.content: The components of data communication are essential for understanding how information is transmitted between devices. A key component is the **Message**, which is the information to be sent, such as text, numbers, pictures, audio, or video [p. 1]. Another is the **Sender**, which is the device that sends the message, like a computer or phone [p. 1]. The **Receiver** is the device that receives the message [p. 1]. The **Transmission medium** is the physical path the message travels, such as twisted pair cable, fiber, or radio waves [p. 1]. A crucial aspect is the **Protocol**, which is the set of rules both sides agree on. Without a protocol, two devices may be connected but cannot understand each other [p. 1]. An example of a protocol is the Internet Protocol (IP) used in the Internet, which works in a **Datagram approach** where each packet is routed on its own and may take a different path .
